newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: World Bank plans $200 mln credit for Kyrgyzstan.
newsitem.headline: World Bank plans $200 mln credit for Kyrgyzstan.

text.p: A senior World Bank official said on Wednesday the bank was ready to provide Kyrgyzstan with a $200 million credit for the development of the Central Asian nation's agriculture, energy and social security sectors.
The bank's vice-president, Johannes Linn, told a news conference Kyrgyzstan was one of the first states with a transition economy to achieve real growth.
Gross domestic product (GDP) in the former Soviet republic has so far grown three percent this year, and Linn said the bank expected GDP growth in 1997 of around 7-8 percent.
The World Bank has already agreed 11 projects worth a total of $395 million.
